title: A twelve-country year on three continents at nearly seventy-four
summary: He travels constantly with Ann in 1978, tiring but undamaged in his playing, and turns seventy-four the next day.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Let's -- at this point, let's also point out some of the absolutely incredible travelling that you've done in the course of all these activities - now, that particular year, which was 1978 that you went down to Buenos Aires - it was a fantastic year in which you played in - I figured it out - on three continents - you played in
twelve countries on three continents in 1978.
Yes - one right after the other.
Yeah. Now, the big thing was you came to this country - after touring Europe you came to this country, toured all over; you played in New York, and then you flew to France for the Nice Festival--
--back to New York and then right straight down to Buenos Aires and then back to this country.
Now, how did all this affect your--did it affect your playing; did it affect the way you felt--
-- From my observation, it didn't affect you a bit--

No - well, if I get a little rest at the end of it - I certainly could jump off of an airplane after being on for 13 hours and expect to play decent-- I was just tired-- in fact, travelling alone makes you tired even if you sleep on the plane; you really don't get the right type of rest. But, it's kind of funny in a way -- a couple of old senior citizens like my wife and me travelling around; we're probably doing more and harder stuff than guys 20 years old would be doing.
